sources.title: The Real Gemstone File · Part One
sources.description: Blog transcription of letters attributed to Bruce Porter Roberts. The supplied page ends mid-sentence on page 26 and marks missing or unreadable material. Initial extraction is selective, not exhaustive. No independent corroboration has yet been added.

people.name: Bruce Porter Roberts
people.description: Author of the letters transcribed on the blog. He frames personal disputes as the entry point to a much broader conspiracy. His causal allegations remain uncorroborated.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: Richard Nixon
people.description: Roberts describes seeking legal help from Nixon before the 1968 election and later sending him demands for federal intervention.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: John Mitchell
people.description: Appears alongside Nixon as an intended recipient of Roberts’ requests for legal representation.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: Joseph Alioto
people.description: Central to Roberts’ account of a September 1968 collision and to his allegations concerning local political influence.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: Ralph Nader
people.description: Recipient of letters connecting Roberts’ claims to Nader’s litigation against General Motors.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: Robert Fellmeth
people.description: Roberts recounts discussions with Fellmeth about his letters and consumer investigations.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: Ted Sorensen
people.description: Spelled Sorenson in the transcription. Roberts links his legal work and Kennedy advisory role to the Nader settlement narrative.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: Simon Rifkind
people.description: Named as Sorensen’s law partner and a participant in the settlement account.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: Arthur Goldberg
people.description: Named in the same legal circle; the letters describe him employing Esther Newberg.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: Edward Kennedy
people.description: Called Teddy throughout the letters. A central figure in Roberts’ unverified interpretation of Chappaquiddick.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: Mary Jo Kopechne
people.description: Her death anchors several threads in Roberts’ narrative. The letters’ claims about motive and conduct are not independently established here.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: John Tunney
people.description: Roberts alleges calls involving Tunney linked California politics to Chappaquiddick.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: Aristotle Onassis
people.description: Placed at the center of the author’s allegations concerning Hughes, money, and political influence.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: Howard Hughes
people.description: The letters allege his empire was taken over and contain conflicting alleged burial dates. Those claims are retained as source claims.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: Robert Maheu
people.description: The source calls him Iron Bob and IBM, and makes unsubstantiated allegations about intelligence operations and assassinations.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: Richard Carlson
people.description: Identified as a writer involved in the Alioto Mafia Web story and a target of Roberts’ attempts to make contact.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: Lance Brisson
people.description: Named alongside Carlson in a public-interest investigation associated with Neilson-Green.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: Mary Pongales
people.description: Roberts describes speaking with her while seeking Carlson in September 1971.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: J. Edgar Hoover
people.description: Named as a recipient of Roberts’ materials and repeatedly associated with the author’s allegations of concealment.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: Noel Gayler
people.description: Roberts recounts a November 1970 visit and a discussion of minerals and possible travel.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: John Mack
people.description: Roberts describes approaching Mack for help and leaving experimental stones with him.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

people.name: John F. Kennedy
people.description: His assassination is woven into the letters’ broader allegations; those alleged connections are unverified.

history.note: Initial profile from the blog transcription; independent verification pending.

events.name: Insurance dispute
events.description: Roberts reports an insurance dispute after a woman entered the path of his car. He later alleges payment despite his winning the case.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.

events.name: The Franklin & Lombard collision
events.description: Roberts alleges an Alioto-family hit-and-run on his car in San Francisco. Pages 3 and 12 give different times: 10:47 and 10:45 p.m. His claims about electoral consequences are uncorroborated.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.

events.name: Seeking help from Nixon
events.description: Roberts recalls approaching candidate Nixon and Mitchell with papers and evidence. The month is given; no exact day is supplied.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.

events.name: 1968 election referenced
events.description: The letters make the election a turning point in Roberts’ account. The date is a normalized calendar date; his claim to have caused the outcome is unverified.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.

events.name: Chappaquiddick
events.description: The letters revisit Kopechne’s death and allege a connection to California political disputes. The calendar date is editorial context; the source’s motive and conspiracy claims are unverified.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.

events.name: Alioto article appears
events.description: Roberts places Carlson’s Look article in August after Chappaquiddick, alleging it concealed his collision account. Exact publication day is not established here.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.

events.name: Roberts’ ultimatum
events.description: Roberts says he submitted an ultimatum to Nixon seeking action on his allegations.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.

events.name: Traffic-court appearance
events.description: Roberts describes dismissal of a traffic ticket and alleges a causal connection to Nixon’s Cambodia decision. This archive does not establish that causal link.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.

events.name: First letter to Nader
events.description: Roberts dates a letter to Nader to the day after a televised interview, and describes calls to two newspapers.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.

events.name: Nader settlement account
events.description: Roberts places a General Motors settlement around August 14 and alleges his letter caused it. The transcription gives both $467,000 and $457,000 in different passages.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.

events.name: Reported visit from Gayler
events.description: Roberts recounts a visit from Gayler concerning minerals and travel. No exact day is given.

events.name: Alleged Hughes burial
events.description: The source alleges burial at sea near Greece, but gives April 16 on page 17 and April 18 on page 12. Neither the death claim nor either date is verified here.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.

events.name: Contact with Neilson-Green
events.description: Roberts recounts contacting the investigation firm in search of Carlson, then speaking with Pongales. His characterization of the firm as a CIA front is unverified.

events.name: November letter to Nader
events.description: A letter heading dates a renewed account addressed to Nader, revisiting the September contact and earlier allegations.

events.name: Proposal for an international inquiry
events.description: Roberts proposes an open, United Nations-based inquiry modeled on the Knapp Commission. This is a proposal, not an established UN proceeding.

events.description: A dated note revisits the Nader settlement, legal relationships and the author’s political allegations.
